top_story_title: Cisco Expressway database-service flaw (CVE-2026-76466) exploited for root access, now KEV-listed
top_story_summary: Cisco Expressway Series devices - Expressway-C and Expressway-E - carry a hard-coded credential / persistent cookie flaw in the database service feature tracked as CVE-2026-76466. An unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to the device and possession of persistent cookies can connect to the database service, invoke specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands, and execute arbitrary operating system commands as root. Cisco's advisory also notes insufficient validation of client certificates when TLS Verify Mode is set to Enabled for clustering, meaning client certificates are not validated.
top_actions: Inventory every Expressway-C and Expressway-E node, including clustered peers and lab or decommission-pending units, and record the running version against the vendor's fixed-release table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
Upgrade to the Cisco fixed release now - the KEV remediation due date is 2026-11-23. Upgrade cluster members in a controlled order and verify cluster health and config sync afterwards.

Until the upgrade lands, restrict the database service and clustering ports so they are reachable only from the cluster peers' addresses, and remove any internet or untrusted-zone path to them with a firewall ACL in front of the DMZ node.
Remove administrative access (HTTPS/SSH/API) from internet-facing interfaces; restrict management to a dedicated management VLAN or out-of-band network and enforce MFA on all admin accounts.

After patching, rotate everything the device held: local admin credentials, API keys, device and clustering certificates, and any service-account or integration credentials configured on Expressway. Invalidate existing sessions and persistent cookies.
executive_summary: Cisco Expressway CVE-2026-76466 is on CISA's KEV list (added 2026-11-20, due 2026-11-23) and confirmed exploited in the wild: unauthenticated root command execution on Expressway-C and Expressway-E via the database service. Patch today and rotate device credentials and certificates.

GreyNoise found an active intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers, with confirmed activity between 17 October and 2 November 2026 affecting at least 22 organizations globally. A compromised management server reaches every gateway it manages - audit it before you audit the gateways.

GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service was compromised and used to install malware on connected routers and KVM devices; users report backdoors and reverse shells. Device count is still unknown and the vendor is still investigating.

Autonomous AI agents on the open-source Cairn framework went from zero-day discovery to root in 11 minutes in real intrusions. Nothing network-specific was targeted, but it sets the patch-window expectation for internet-facing edge devices.

The same KEV batch added CVE-2026-123890, a VMware vCenter authentication bypass exploited as a zero-day for months. Not a network device, but it will compete for the same maintenance window this week.
key_actions: **Cisco** — Identify all Expressway-C and Expressway-E nodes from asset inventory, filtered by model and running version, and compare against the vendor's fixed-release table; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release.
**Cisco** — Apply the Cisco fixed release inside the change window today - the KEV remediation date is 2026-11-23 - or record the deviation with a compensating control.
**Cisco** — Read the advisory and map your running train to the fixed release before scheduling; check the vendor advisory for the fixed release rather than assuming the latest build.
**Cisco** — Upgrade all cluster members and verify cluster state and configuration sync after the upgrade.
**GL.iNet** — Locate every GL.iNet router or KVM in use, including user-purchased travel routers used for remote work, and determine whether each is enrolled in GoodCloud.
**GL.iNet** — Disconnect affected devices from the cloud management service and disable cloud/remote management until the vendor confirms the service is clean.

**Check Point** — Read the GreyNoise report and block or hunt its published C2 addresses in firewall and proxy logs covering at least 17 October to 2 November 2026 - retrospectively, not just going forward.

**Check Point** — Treat this as an incident review on the management server, not a patch task: check for unexpected administrator accounts, unexplained policy installs, new or modified scripts, and SmartConsole or API logins outside change windows.

headlines.title: Cisco Expressway vulnerability exploited to breach internal networks (CVE-2026-76466)
headlines.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-76466 to its KEV catalog after attackers used the Cisco Expressway database-service flaw to run commands as root and breach internal networks.

headlines.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
headlines.summary: Cisco's advisory details unauthenticated root command execution in the Expressway database service, reachable with persistent cookies against clustered Expressway-C and Expressway-E.

headlines.title: GL.iNet cloud compromise hits routers and KVMs, older backdoors also found
headlines.summary: Attackers compromised GL.iNet's GoodCloud remote management service and used it to install malware on connected routers and KVM devices.

headlines.title: 99 IPs but a C2 ain’t one: An Active Intrusion Campaign Against Check Point Security Management Servers
headlines.summary: GreyNoise found an intrusion campaign against Check Point Security Management Servers affecting at least 22 organizations globally.

headlines.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
headlines.summary: CISA warned federal agencies that the critical Cisco Expressway remote code execution flaw is being exploited in the wild.

headlines.title: Hackers exploit GL.iNet cloud flaw to infect routers, KVM devices
headlines.summary: GL.iNet confirmed attackers abused a flaw in its cloud management service to install custom malware, with users finding backdoors and reverse shells on routers.
